name: Anti-patriotism
summary: Anti-patriotism rejects patriotism as an arbitrary and harmful attachment: people do not choose their birth country, yet are taught to love it and die for it. Its classic critics argue that patriotism feeds militarism, conscription and war, serves rulers and the wealthy, and divides people who share interests across borders. They call instead for universal brotherhood and international solidarity.
scope: The classic critique as made by Emma Goldman (Patriotism: A Menace to Liberty, 1910) and Leo Tolstoy (Patriotism and Government, 1900), with the anarchist, Marxist-internationalist and cosmopolitan strands the Wikipedia overview names, including Kotoku Shusui. Anti-patriotism is a stance on loyalty, not a full programme, so answers on economics and social questions are inferred from these strands and mostly low confidence. It excludes constitutional patriotism and critical patriotism, which defend patriotism in revised form.

sources.title: Anti-patriotism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition, strands (anarchist, Marxist, Kotoku Shusui) and links to cosmopolitanism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a patriotism question; the anarchist and socialist strands the profile draws on favour common provision of basic needs, though not necessarily through a state.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Anarchist and Tolstoyan strands distrust both corporations and the regulatory state, so the answer is split.

worker-ownership.rationale: Goldman's anarchist and Marxist currents favour workers controlling production; not a core anti-patriotic claim.

strong-leader.rationale: Tolstoy argues power concentrates at the apex of government and falls to the unscrupulous, and Goldman demands no loyal obedience; both reject leaders bypassing checks.

state-harmful.rationale: Tolstoy holds that government rests on violence and that abolishing its instruments would not make things worse; anarchists in the strand agree, though Marxist adherents do not.

limit-guns.rationale: Goldman opposes the militarised state, yet anarchists also support armed workers; adherents split.

empower-police-military.rationale: Goldman calls the standing army a justification for spending and calls militarism capitalism's greatest bulwark; Tolstoy calls arms races endless.

traditional-family.rationale: Goldman was a radical critic of conventional family and marriage in her wider work, but this essay does not address it.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Goldman rejects the nation as the unit of loyalty and calls patriotic pride a conceit, so valuing national culture as such is disfavoured, though local tradition is not attacked.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The strand's world-citizen and cosmopolitan outlook, with Goldman's image of nations as iron-gated spots, opposes national exclusion.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Tolstoy mocks the Hague conferences as futile while internationalists value cooperation; anarchists distrust any new power centre.

free-trade.rationale: Cosmopolitans like open exchange but Goldman blames capitalist interests for wars; adherents split.

nation-first.rationale: Tolstoy defines patriotism as seeking advantage for one's own state at the expense of other peoples and calls it immoral; putting country first is exactly what is rejected.

open-borders.rationale: Goldman's picture of a world cut into iron-gated nations and her call for universal brotherhood point toward dissolving borders; the Wikipedia article stresses world citizenship.

limit-growth.rationale: No link to the sources; adherents split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Goldman's anarchist and Marxist currents expect social revolution, but Tolstoy preferred nonviolent refusal, so the answer is a qualified yes.

central-planning.rationale: Anarchist and Tolstoyan strands reject state direction of the economy, though Marxists differ.

socialized-markets.rationale: No stated position; the strands sampled are split between markets and moneyless communism.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Anarcho-communist adherents favour it, as the Wikipedia article notes; the essay itself does not discuss it.

one-party-rule.rationale: Tolstoy and Goldman oppose concentrated rule and demanded loyalty, and the Wikipedia article lists opposition to authoritarianism.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Tolstoy blames rulers and their instruments for sustaining patriotism and war, so hereditary rule gets no legitimacy.

democracy-best.rationale: Tolstoy saw all government as violence, while some Marxist and liberal strands accept democracy; adherents split.

direct-votes.rationale: Anarchists prefer direct participation but reject voting as the mechanism; split.

workers-councils.rationale: Marxist and anarchist adherents favour councils over parliaments; the source texts do not discuss it.

natural-rulers.rationale: Tolstoy shows power passing to the least scrupulous, and the strand's egalitarianism denies a natural class of rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Tolstoy was a strict pacifist while Goldman's anarchist currents sometimes accepted revolutionary violence; adherents split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Goldman describes war as a quarrel between thieves sending others' sons to die and barracks as degrading soldiers; Tolstoy calls war a product of patriotism.

military-superiority.rationale: Tolstoy argues arms races escalate without limit and that nations cannot trust each other while armies exist; Goldman calls defence spending a myth.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Goldman rejects nationalist divisions of humanity and calls for universal brotherhood.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Goldman's workers' solidarity and the Marxist strand support a class reading of history, though Tolstoy did not.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Anti-statist and anti-colonial adherents lean yes; the sources do not take it up.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Goldman's anarchism rests on solidarity, though she prized individual freedom; split but leans no.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Goldman says patriotism turns a thinking being into a loyal machine denied rights; she objects to subordinating the individual.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Tolstoy was sympathetic to simple life but the strand includes industrial socialists; split.

restore-past-order.rationale: Tolstoy treats patriotism as a relic of older ideas on the way out in favour of brotherhood, so nostalgia for lost order is rejected.

direct-action.rationale: Goldman praises soldiers refusing orders and workers refusing to kill, and Tolstoy urges refusing enlistment and taxes; the strands favour refusal over elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Tolstoy argues that peace comes from refusing violent institutions, not using them; Goldman's anarchism holds a similar line.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Kropotkin-style anarchists discuss it but the sources do not; split.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Anarchist and Tolstoyan strands reject state power even in workers' hands, though Marxist adherents accept it; leans no.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Goldman traces the Spanish-American and Russo-Japanese wars to capitalist interests and calls militarism capitalism's bulwark, but Tolstoy blames patriotism and governments rather than capitalism, so 'inevitably' is stronger than the tradition as a whole.

taxation-theft.rationale: Tolstoy urged refusing war taxes but not all taxes; individualist and communist anarchists differ.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Goldman defends the individual against the state while championing class solidarity; split.

conscription.rationale: Tolstoy says conscription turns citizens into submissive slaves, and Goldman condemns the military law drafting citizens.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Goldman's anti-state view values leaving but the strand also seeks collective change; split.

media-academia-power.rationale: Tolstoy blames the press and schools for propagating patriotism, but for elite interests rather than their own power; leans no.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Goldman's universal brotherhood and rejection of national superiority exclude racial hierarchy.

total-state.rationale: Goldman condemns demanded unquestioned obedience and the state training children in militarism; Tolstoy opposes concentrated power.

national-rebirth.rationale: Goldman calls patriotism a superstition built on conceit and lies, so a radical national revival is rejected.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Wikipedia article cites Kōtoku's attack on imperialism, and Tolstoy calls national advantage at others' expense immoral.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Goldman rejects oaths of loyalty and obedience as making people machines.

universal-morality.rationale: The SEP notes the universalist tradition treats patriotism as arbitrary partiality conflicting with universal justice, which anti-patriots build on.

rule-by-example.rationale: Tolstoy rejects government by force but not moral example as such; the claim is about rulers, so doubtful.

national-self-determination.rationale: Goldman and Tolstoy reject the nation as the unit of loyalty; self-determination is a national-state right they would not defend, though anti-colonial adherents may.

force-without-un.rationale: Tolstoy opposes states using force for advantage and Goldman calls wars theft quarrels; unilateral force is rejected.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Tolstoy was a religious thinker and Goldman a freethinker; split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Reserving benefits for citizens is national exclusion; the strand's cosmopolitanism rejects it.

class-collaboration.rationale: Goldman stresses that workers' interests lie against their wealthy compatriots, not in partnership with them.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-imperial but blocs make new rival camps; adherents split.

workers-nation.rationale: Goldman says workers share interests across borders more than with their rich compatriots and calls for an international feeling of solidarity.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Goldman's work opposed enforced gender roles and the strand is egalitarian; the essay does not address it directly.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Goldman shows troops used against strikes and a state demanding loyalty for the wealthy, matching the instrument-of-class view.

elite-replacement.rationale: This conspiracy view treats nations as peoples to defend, opposite to the strand's universal brotherhood.

national-mission.rationale: Tolstoy says every patriot thinks his country the best and Goldman says each people believes its land makes it superior; a national mission is exactly that conceit.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Radical adherents lean yes; Goldman wrote on this elsewhere but not in the essay.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Tolstoy argues the apex of power falls to unscrupulous people, and Goldman says governments exploit patriotism for the rich.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Defence and enforcing property are the very functions Goldman calls a pretext; adherents want less state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Goldman's call for universal brotherhood and rejection of each nation's superiority rests on the equality of all people.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The strand's internationalism points to socialism being international, though anarchist adherents do not use this framing.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Tolstoy argues governments provoke enmity to rally their people, and Goldman denies the defence rationale; strengthening the state is rejected.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export drives are economic nationalism that the strand opposes; Goldman ties national economic rivalry to war.

population-transfer.rationale: Goldman condemns national division and calls for universal brotherhood; forcing a minority out is the opposite.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Tolstoy's strict nonresistance supports it, but anarchist adherents accept revolutionary force; leans yes.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Tolstoy holds that humanity advances toward brotherhood of peoples, and Goldman rejects nationalist rivalry as the driver of anything good.

separated-powers.rationale: Tolstoy rejects government as such, so checks within the state are not his concern; split.

vanguard-party.rationale: Anarchist and Tolstoyan adherents reject vanguards, while Leninists differ; leans no.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Goldman cites troops used against strikers and praises soldiers who refused; restricting strikes is opposed. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Goldman rejects national homogeneity as a good and calls for universal brotherhood.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Goldman's Buwalda example shows state punishing dissent in the name of national need; adherents reject suspending protections.

party-controls-media.rationale: Tolstoy blames state-run press and schools for spreading patriotism; control by the ruling party is rejected.

party-commands-army.rationale: Goldman opposes the army and loyalty to the ruling power; a party-commanded army is rejected.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The Wikipedia article notes some anti-patriots fold European identity into national identity; supranational pooling is favoured over national sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Goldman criticises the president directing citizens into military service; executive command of forces is rejected.

clerical-rule.rationale: Tolstoy criticises the church as promoting patriotism for privilege; clerical rule is rejected.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Goldman urges workers to refuse to kill for their masters and Tolstoy urges refusing military service; neither calls for working toward one's own government's defeat, which is a Leninist position.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Goldman defended free expression against state suppression; censoring art is rejected.

people-in-arms.rationale: Goldman rejects the standing army yet the strand does not endorse arming the citizenry for national defence; split.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Tolstoy idealised peasant life but the strand does not require it; split.

death-penalty.rationale: Goldman notes American hypocrisy over violence including executions of workers; Tolstoy was strongly opposed.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The Wikipedia article stresses that people do not choose their birth country; descent-based citizenship deepens nationality. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Goldman defends individual liberty against state coercion and attacks the state's demand for obedience.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Tolstoy argues arms races escalate endlessly and Goldman calls defence spending a pretext; national nuclear arms are rejected.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Goldman calls national claims to land a conceit; nothing in the strand supports holding land at the cost of peace.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anarchist adherents hold this; Marxist-Leninists do not, so confidence is low.

collective-defense.rationale: Goldman denies that standing armies serve defence and sees wars as quarrels of thieves; allied obligations to fight are rejected.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The strand distrusts both church and state power; no stated view.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Tolstoy rejects violence by states to hold subjects together; Goldman rejects the loyalty demand.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Tolstoy calls patriotism hypnotism sustained by rulers, and rejects the elevation of rulers; sacred rulers are rejected.

leader-cult.rationale: Goldman says patriotism requires allegiance to symbols and turns people into loyal machines; Tolstoy attacks the hypnotism that props up rulers.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Goldman rejects nationalist divisions of the world; irredentist claims are the extreme of that.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Tolstoy opposed armed groups while insurrectionary anarchists favoured them; split.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Goldman and Tolstoy attack privilege defended in the name of the nation; Wikipedia notes the equality motive.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Tolstoy blames schools for teaching patriotism and Goldman accuses schools of glorifying war; nation-centred history is rejected.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Wikipedia article cites Kōtoku's condemnation of imperialism; rule over others is rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: Goldman says schools train children in military tactics and war glorification; Tolstoy names schools as patriotism's instrument.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The Wikipedia article cites Kōtoku's attack on imperialism; cultivating influence over former colonies is rejected.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Goldman stresses cross-border worker solidarity, which is hard to square with labour aristocracy; split.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Egalitarianism conflicts with it; libertarian adherents differ; leans no.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Goldman defends rights against the state; anarchists distrust constitutions; split.

elective-rulers.rationale: Tolstoy rejects rulers entirely; Marxists accept election; split.

minority-veto.rationale: Consensus-minded anarchists agree, others differ; split.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Tolstoy rejects the state in any form, so which branch rules is not a concern; split.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Tolstoy was a vegetarian and anarchists commonly agree, but the essays do not address it.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Goldman and Tolstoy urged active refusal rather than withdrawal; Tolstoy leaned toward withdrawal from state institutions, so leaning no.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Tolstoy argues press, church and schools hypnotise people into patriotism to protect privilege, which is close to this claim.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Tolstoy says officials, press, church and schools promote patriotism to protect their privileges, a consent-through-culture account.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving office by birth makes birthplace decisive, which the strand rejects.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Goldman calls national pride a conceit and wars economic quarrels; claiming territory back by demand is rejected.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anarchist adherents may agree, Marxists do not; split.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Goldman calls militarism capitalism's bulwark and the army a pretext for spending; a political guardian army is rejected.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Tolstoy condemns states pursuing advantage by force; arming proxies is rejected.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Tolstoy opposes great powers using force for their interests; Goldman condemns imperial wars.

democratic-peace.rationale: Tolstoy rejected the premise that governments cause peace; liberal view differs; split.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Goldman denounces the demand for unquestioned obedience and Tolstoy urges refusal to enlist and pay war taxes.

non-intervention.rationale: Tolstoy rejects state force but anarchist solidarity favours aid; split.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Goldman's rejection of national conceit and call for universal brotherhood excludes scapegoating minorities.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Placing the nation's law over international law is national supremacy that the strand rejects.

religious-nation.rationale: Goldman and Tolstoy reject definitions of the nation by loyalty, and Tolstoy's brotherhood is universal.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tolstoy rejects states demanding advantage over others; ritual tribute is rejected.

defeat-communism.rationale: Tolstoy and Goldman oppose war as policy; waging struggle to defeat a rival system is rejected.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marxists agree and Tolstoy was devout; split.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Goldman's closing vision of a free society uniting people, and anarchist adherents favour cooperative communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-encouraged settlement to dominate minority regions is national conquest; Goldman rejects it.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Anarchists agree, Marxists do not; split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Goldman calls attachment to national soil a conceit; historical claims are rejected.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The strand's universal brotherhood excludes it; no adherent line supports it. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Goldman cites the state punishing dissent and demanding unquestioned obedience; suppression is rejected.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Wikipedia article cites Kōtoku's attack on imperialism as a monster of the century.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Goldman's universal brotherhood excludes civilisational incompatibility claims. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Tolstoy was a Christian anarchist denying state legitimacy, though not by denying God; leans no for the strand.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Tolstoy argues nations cannot trust each other while armies exist and urges refusing enlistment; Goldman attacks the standing army as a myth.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Tolstoy and Goldman oppose bloc wars; staying out is closer than joining, though they would go further.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Tolstoy attacks rulers as instruments of the patriotic state; dynastic rule is rejected. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist anarchists favour it; others silent; split.

property-franchise.rationale: Goldman sided with workers against the wealthy; property qualifications are rejected.

racial-franchise.rationale: Goldman's universal brotherhood excludes racial voting rights.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Goldman rejects nationalist hostility, and universal brotherhood excludes it.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Goldman links wealth to militarism and governments serving the rich.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Adherents oppose the military; liberty favours it but the army is rejected; split.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Tolstoy favoured voluntary aid, Marxists do not; split.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Cosmopolitan outlook disfavours birth-based exclusion from civic life. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Goldman condemns schools training children in military tactics and glorifying war.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Tolstoy and Goldman oppose militarism; the question assumes weapons, which they would remove.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Goldman denounces military spending as a pretext; foreign bases are part of that apparatus.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Goldman sides with workers against the wealthy who profit from their labour.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Tolstoy held it strictly while anarchist adherents did not; split.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Goldman calls patriotism a superstition built on lies; invented continuity is part of it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Goldman describes patriotism as asking people to die for conceit and Kateb notes readiness to die and kill for an abstraction.

independent-unions.rationale: Goldman praises workers acting independently of their masters and the state.

person-over-state.rationale: Goldman says patriotism turns a thinking being into a loyal machine and denies a soldier his rights as a human being.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Tolstoy affirmed it while materialists in the strand did not; split.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Goldman's call for universal brotherhood and worker unity across borders rejects organising by race.

racial-pride.rationale: Goldman calls pride in birthplace or nation a conceit; race-based pride is the same sentiment.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Goldman denies that standing armies defend, and Tolstoy rejects war entirely; moderate patriotic view is not theirs.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Defining nations by language accepts the nation as the unit of belonging, which anti-patriots reject.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Goldman describes national fears as myths maintained to frighten the foolish.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.

reviewHistory.rationale: Pacifist feminism links women to peace but the essay does not; split.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

arms-reduction.rationale: Tolstoy and Goldman want armies and armaments done away with altogether and reject the 'national safety' rationale; they support cutting arms, but not on the statement's terms.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Goldman describes wars concocted through lies and capitalist interests; openness follows.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Goldman praises soldiers who refused to fire on strikers and Tolstoy urges refusing enlistment as the way to end war.

sacred-nation.rationale: Goldman calls patriotism a superstition and Tolstoy calls it immoral, so treating the nation as sacred is what they reject.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Tolstoy was a religious universalist but Goldman an atheist; the strands split and patriotism is the focus.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Goldman and Tolstoy blame patriotism for militarism and arms build-up and call for disarmament and refusal of war, so a state keeping weapons against rivals is the patriotic logic they reject. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

workers-own-party.rationale: Marxist strands favor workers' parties while anarchist strands like Goldman reject parliamentary parties; the strands split.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Not a patriotism question; the anarchist and Marxist strands include both voluntarist and union-solidarity views.

national-church-status.rationale: Tolstoy denounces the Church as serving government and Goldman rejects state-backed institutions of loyalty, so special legal status for a national church is opposed.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Goldman and Tolstoy reject love of a birth country as an arbitrary superstition and deny any duty to defend it.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Tolstoy holds that conscience outranks government commands, and Goldman urges refusal of unjust duties; this supports the claim, though neither addresses law directly.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Marxist strands accept the labour theory of value while anarchist and Tolstoyan strands do not discuss it; the strands split.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The defining claim is that patriotism divides workers who share interests across borders; Goldman says patriotism serves capital and sets workers against each other.

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: The Wikipedia article cites Kōtoku's attack on imperialism; cultivating influence over former colonies is rejected. (Carried over from former-empire-influence, "A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Loyalty to one's own country is a moral virtue.
missingStatements.rationale: Goldman calls patriotism a superstition resting on conceit, and Tolstoy calls it immoral, so the defining claim is that loyalty to country is not a virtue.

missingStatements.text: Soldiers should refuse orders to fight in wars between states.
missingStatements.rationale: Goldman praises soldiers who refused to fire on strikers and Tolstoy urges refusing enlistment as the way to end war.

notes: Most answers are inferred, because anti-patriotism is a stance on loyalty and not a programme. Adherents range from anarchist and Marxist internationalists to Tolstoyan pacifists, and these differ on revolution, the state and violence.
